27	\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,itemsep=2pt]
28	    \item A systematic study of ontological constraint violations in LLM-based IE: rates are driven by constraint tightness rather than ontology scale, and prompt-level intervention is per-relation unreliable.
29	    \item OntoCoDec, a two-layer framework compiling ontology schemas into stateful logit masks that enforce pair-based domain/range constraints during autoregressive IE, unlike code generation where types are statically declared.
30	    \item Near-lossless composability with LoRA across RE and EE: DR\,$\leq$\,0.20\% at $<$0.6\,pp F1 cost on RE, RoV$\to$0\% and AC$\leq$0.8\% on EE. Zero-shot robustness across four models (8B--70B) and three datasets: DR $\downarrow$42--99\%, WikiEvents violations $\to$0\%; 70B achieves DR$\to$0\% on both RE datasets.
31	    \item Analysis of the CF$\leftrightarrow$DR trade-off in per-slot enforcement (resolved to CF\,$\leq$\,1.2\% by fine-tuning); beam search ($k{=}4$) eliminates all four violation types under fine-tuned decoding (SciERC, both Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B).

    "originalFile": "% Section 5 — SciERC Results (Draft)\n% Data source: Phase 2 SciERC registry experiments\n% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_unconstrained, phase2_scierc_grammar_only,\n%          phase2_scierc_semantic_only, phase2_scierc_full_s1, phase2_scierc_full_s2\n% All numbers verified against registry 2026-05-14.\n\n\\subsection{Ablation and Composability with Fine-Tuning}\n\\label{sec:scierc-results}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:scierc-ablation} presents the five-way ablation on SciERC (Qwen3-8B, zero-shot, 551 documents); only the active constraint layers differ across rows.\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n%  Table: SciERC five-way ablation\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{3.6pt}\n\\resizebox{\\columnwidth}{!}{%\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}l rrrrrr rr@{}}\n\\toprule\n& \\multicolumn{6}{c}{\\textbf{Violation Rates (\\%)}}\n& \\multicolumn{2}{c}{\\textbf{F1}} \\\\\n\\cmidrule(lr){2-7} \\cmidrule(l){8-9}\n\\textbf{Mode}\n  & DR\\,$\\downarrow$ & $\\Delta$DR\n  & RV\\,$\\downarrow$ & ET\\,$\\downarrow$ & CF & Tot.\\,$\\downarrow$\n  & Rel.\\,$\\uparrow$ & Ent.\\,$\\uparrow$ \\\\\n\\midrule\nUnconstrained\n  & 15.37 & ---\n  & 1.39  & 0.40\n  & 0.08  & 15.45\n  & 8.23  & 31.01 \\\\\nGrammar\n  & 14.84 & $\\downarrow$3\\%\n  & \\textbf{0} & \\textbf{0}\n  & 0.08  & 14.92\n  & 8.23  & 30.98 \\\\\nSemantic\n  & 11.65 & $\\downarrow$24\\%\n  & 1.51  & 0.40\n  & 2.71  & 14.36\n  & 8.15  & 31.01 \\\\\nFull (S1)\n  & \\textbf{0.93} & $\\downarrow$\\textbf{94\\%}\n  & \\textbf{0} & \\textbf{0}\n  & 9.90  & \\textbf{10.83}\n  & \\textbf{8.36} & 30.98 \\\\\nFull (S2)\n  & 0.97  & $\\downarrow$94\\%\n  & \\textbf{0} & \\textbf{0}\n  & 8.03  & \\textbf{9.00}\n  & 8.03  & \\textbf{31.90} \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}}%\n\\caption{Five-way ablation on SciERC (551 docs, Qwen3-8B, zero-shot).\n$\\Delta$DR: relative change vs.\\ unconstrained.\nTot.\\ = DR + CF (total type-violation burden).\nBest per column in \\textbf{bold} (CF excluded; Tot.\\ included).\nF1 $\\times$100. Bootstrap: 10{,}000 iterations.}\n\\label{tab:scierc-ablation}\n\\end{table}\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n%  (a) Core result\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\paragraph{Zero-shot diagnostic.}\n% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: DR=0.1537; phase2_scierc_full_s1: DR=0.0093\n% phase2_scierc_unconstrained: R-F1=0.0823; phase2_scierc_full_s1: R-F1=0.0836\n% bootstrap: delta=+0.13pp, CI=[-0.24,+0.58], p=0.5824\nFull S1 reduces DR from 15.37\\% to 0.93\\% ($\\downarrow$94\\%) while R-F1 is unchanged (8.23\\,$\\to$\\,8.36, $p{=}0.58$).\nPer-relation DR drops to $\\leq$2.82\\%, reaching 0\\% on 4/7 relations (Appendix~\\ref{app:per-relation-landscape}).\nPost-hoc filtering achieves slightly higher F1 via precision gains but discards up to 48\\% of predictions including true positives (Appendix~\\ref{app:posthoc-extended}).\nCF rises from 0.08\\% to 9.90\\% (\\S\\ref{sec:discussion}).\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n%  (b) Grammar layer\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\paragraph{Layer contributions.}\n% phase2_scierc_grammar_only: RV=0, ET=0, DR=0.1484, R-F1=0.0823\nGrammar-only eliminates RV and ET with no F1 impact while DR remains at 14.84\\%, the ceiling of grammar-based decoding~\\cite{geng2023gcd}; grammar-only CF is near-zero (0.08\\%), so CF originates from the semantic layer.\nSemantic-only reduces DR by only 24\\% and cannot eliminate RV or ET — the \\emph{enabling dependency}: adding the grammar layer yields a further 92\\% reduction (11.65\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0.93\\%).\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n%  (d) S1 vs S2\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\paragraph{S1 vs.\\ S2.}\nS2 achieves comparable DR (0.97\\%) but lower R-F1 (8.03 vs.\\ 8.36) with fewer triples (1{,}644 vs.\\ 1{,}729) and does not resolve the CF trade-off (8.03\\% vs.\\ 9.90\\%); we adopt S1 as the primary configuration.\n% phase2_scierc_full_s2: DR=0.0097, R-F1=0.0803, CF=0.0803, triples=1644\n\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n%  (e) Composability with Fine-Tuning\n%  exp_ids: lora_scierc_unconstrained, lora_scierc_full_s1\n% ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\\paragraph{Composability with fine-tuning.}\n\\label{sec:composability}\n% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_unconstrained, phase2_scierc_full_s1,\n%          w5_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_lora_scierc_constrained_eval,\n%          llama_scierc_unconstrained, llama_scierc_full_s1,\n%          w5_llama_lora_scierc_unconstrained_eval, w5_llama_lora_scierc_constrained_eval\nFine-tuning alone reduces DR to 1--2\\% but leaves residual violations (Table~\\ref{tab:composability}).\nAdding S1: Qwen DR 1.95\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0\\%, Llama 1.11\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0.09\\% on SciERC; Qwen 0.76\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0.01\\%, Llama 0.49\\%\\,$\\to$\\,0.20\\% on DocRED.\n% w5_qwen_docred_lora_constrained_eval: DR=0.01%, R-F1=40.56; w5_llama_docred_lora_constrained_eval: DR=0.20%, R-F1=44.23\nAcross all settings, DR\\,$\\leq$\\,0.20\\% with R-F1 within $\\pm$0.6\\,pp.\nCF interference drops from $+$9.82\\,pp (zero-shot) to $+$1.18\\,pp (fine-tuned), tracing to \\textsc{Generic}$\\leftrightarrow$X ambiguity (Appendix~\\ref{app:cf-distribution}).\nBeam search ($k{=}4$) eliminates residual DR and CF to $<$1\\% (Appendix~\\ref{app:beam-search}).\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{3pt}\n\\resizebox{\\columnwidth}{!}{%\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}lll rrrr 从 KAIROS 约束文件计算每个 role 的 constraint tightness κ(role) = 1 - |valid_entity_types(role)| / |total_entity_types|。

步骤：
1. 在远程服务器找到 WikiEvents 的约束文件（类似 `event_role_KAIROS.json` 或 `ontology_constraints.json`，在 `/root/schema_semantic_constrained_ie/` 下搜索）
2. 对每个 role，统计允许的 entity type 数量
3. 总 entity type 数 = 27（已知）
4. 计算 κ(role) 并输出：min/max/mean/median κ，以及与 zero-shot AC 率的定性关系
5. 输出 top-5 最紧和最松的 role 及其 κ 值

**Task 2: EE FT CF 计算 (W5)**
从 EE FT 推理输出 JSONL 计算 cross-field consistency violation rate。

定义：同一文档内，同一 entity text 在不同 event argument 中被标注为不同 type = 1 次 CF violation。

步骤：
1. 找到 EE FT 输出文件：
   - Qwen: westd-21461 上 p1_ee_ft_composability_r5 的 constrained 输出
   - Llama: westd-16980 上 p1_ee_ft_llama_r2 的 constrained 输出
2. 写 Python 脚本计算 CF：遍历每个 doc 的所有 event arguments，对同一 entity text 检查 type 是否一致
3. 报告：Qwen CF%, Llama CF%，以及 unconstrained 的 CF%（如果有输出文件）

两个任务独立，可以用两个 Worker 并行。结果汇报给我，我再派 Paper Agent 入稿。

Llama FT unconstrained 输出\n\n### Step 2: 理解输出格式\n\n先读取一个文件的前几行理解 JSON 结构：\n```bash\nhead -2 &lt;output_file> | python3 -m json.tool\n```\n\nEE 输出的结构可能是：\n```json\n{\n  \"events\": [\n    {\n      \"event_type\": \"...\",\n      \"trigger\": \"...\",\n      \"arguments\": [\n        {\"role\": \"...\", \"entity_text\": \"...\", \"entity_type\": \"...\"},\n        ...\n      ]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n或者可能在 \"prediction\" / \"output\" 等字段下。先确认实际结构。\n\n### Step 3: 写 CF 计算脚本\n\n在任一服务器上写 `/root/schema_semantic_constrained_ie/scripts/calc_ee_cf.py`：\n\n```python\nimport json\nimport sys\nfrom collections import Counter\n\ndef calc_cf(filepath):\n    \"\"\"计算 EE 输出的 CF violation rate\"\"\"\n    total_docs = 0\n    total_entities = 0  # entity-role assignments\n    cf_violations = 0\n    docs_with_cf = 0\n    \n    with open(filepath) as f:\n        for line in f:\n            doc = json.loads(line)\n            total_docs += 1\n            \n            # 收集所有 (entity_text, entity_type) pairs\n            # 需要根据实际结构调整字段名\n            entity_types = {}  # entity_text -> set of types\n            \n            # 遍历所有 events 和 arguments\n            events = doc.get('events', doc.get('prediction', {}).get('events', []))\n            for event in events:\n                args = event.get('arguments', [])\n                for arg in args:\n                    text = arg.get('entity_text', arg.get('text', '')).strip().lower()\n                    etype = arg.get('entity_type', arg.get('type', ''))\n                    if text and etype:\n                        total_entities += 1\n                        if text not in entity_types:\n                            entity_types[text] = set()\n                        entity_types[text].add(etype)\n            \n            # CF = entity text 有多于 1 种 type\n            doc_cf = sum(1 for types in entity_types.values() if len(types) > 1)\n            if doc_cf > 0:\n                cf_violations += doc_cf\n                docs_with_cf += 1\n    \n    cf_rate = cf_violations / total_entities * 100 if total_entities > 0 else 0\n    return {\n        'total_docs': total_docs,\n        'total_entity_assignments': total_entities,\n        'cf_entities': cf_violations,\n        'docs_with_cf': docs_with_cf,\n        'cf_rate_pct': cf_rate\n    }\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    filepath = sys.argv[1]\n    result = calc_cf(filepath)\n    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))\n```\n\n**重要**: 先读取实际文件格式，再调整字段名。EE 输出的结构可能与 RE 不同。\n\n### Step 4: 在所有文件上运行\n\n对 4 个文件分别运行脚本，收集结果。\n\n### Step 5: 也检查已有的 violation report\n\n可能之前的 violation checker 已经计算了 CF。检查：\n```bash\nls outputs/violation_report*ee*ft* outputs/violation_report*wiki*ft* 2>/dev/null\ncat &lt;violation_report_file> | python3 -c \"import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(json.dumps({k:v for k,v in d.items() if 'cf' in k.lower() or 'cross' in k.lower()}, indent=2))\"\n```\n\n### 产出\n\n写本地 artifact: `/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_6/projects/schema_semantic_constrained_ie/artifacts/w5_ee_ft_cf_results.md`\n\n包含：\n\n| Model | Condition | Total Args | CF Entities | CF Rate (%) |\n|-------|-----------|-----------|-------------|-------------|\n| Qwen | Unconstrained | ? | ? | ? |\n| Qwen | Constrained | ? | ? | ? |\n| Llama | Unconstrained | ? | ? | ? |\n| Llama | Constrained | ? | ? | ? |\n\n以及：\n- CF 来源分析（哪些 entity text 最常有 type 不一致）\n- 与 RE CF rate 的对比（RE constrained CF: Qwen 1.18%, Llama 0.46% on SciERC）\n"

127	### Qualitative Analysis
128	
129	1. **Tight constraints amplify violations**: The κ ≥ 0.90 group has the highest AC violation rate (50%), significantly above the medium group (21%). When only 1-2 entity types are valid, LLMs are much more likely to assign an incorrect type. This is especially pronounced for "Crime" roles (only CRM valid) and "BodyPart" (only BOD valid), where models consistently produce PER or other common types instead.
130	
131	2. **Non-monotonic pattern in loose group**: The loose κ < 0.80 group shows 30% AC rate, higher than the medium group. This is driven primarily by Attack.Unspecified.Target (126 args, 34% AC rate, κ=0.5926) and GenericCrime.Victim (14 args, 64% AC rate, κ=0.8148). These are high-frequency roles where the model makes systematic errors despite relatively permissive constraints.
132	
133	3. **Role semantics interact with tightness**: Some very tight roles have 0% AC violation (Transportation.Vehicle, BlockPassage.Vehicle, Crash.Vehicle) because "VEH" is semantically obvious. In contrast, abstract roles like "Crime" (valid: CRM only) or "Sentence" (valid: SEN only) have near-100% AC violations because LLMs don't distinguish fine-grained KAIROS types (CRM, SEN) from common types (PER, ORG).
134	
135	4. **Key insight for the paper**: κ is necessary but not sufficient to predict violation rate. The interaction between constraint tightness and entity type "prototypicality" (how often LLMs default to common types like PER/ORG/GPE) determines actual violation rates. This supports the motivation for semantic-constrained decoding: tighter constraints create more opportunities for violation, but only when the valid types are non-prototypical.
